title: Representational Relativity

hero.headline: The representation changes. The invariant is what survives lawful transport.
hero.support: A recovered public-facing frame for the principle that no representation is the thing itself: each carrier exposes, compresses, distorts, or preserves structure according to its boundary and context.

sections.heading: Representations are interfaces
sections.body: A representation is not a passive copy. It mediates what can be seen, compared, transported, acted upon, and forgotten.

sections.heading: Carriers can change
sections.body: Text, diagrams, software objects, measurements, legal categories, models, performances, and human descriptions may carry the same object differently.

sections.heading: Validity is transport
sections.body: The important question is which distinctions and invariants survive admissible movement between representations.

sections.heading: Defects appear at the crossing
sections.body: A representational defect occurs when a distinction that consequence still depends on is lost, invented, collapsed, or moved without warrant.

sections.heading: Current formal home
sections.body: The underlying principle now belongs inside Representational Mechanics, with closure gauges and admissible distinction providing more precise machinery.

notes: Recovered from the earlier eight-page landing-page set.
